name: parameterised-card
title: Host-parameterised profile card
summary: A profile card whose name, subtitle, accent colour and progress are exported host variables with good defaults, so it renders well with no host and re-renders when the host sets them.
prompt: Make a profile card template where the app can set the name, subtitle, accent colour and progress, and it still looks right with no data.
teaches: Export a float to the host with resources.variables {"progress": {"value": 0.65, "export": true}}
Export a colour with resources.colors (named colours are exported by default) and use it as "@colors.accent" in backgrounds and paints
Export a string with a root variable {"vtype": "string", "export": true} and show it with text value "@name"
Give host-supplied strings maxLines 1 and an ellipsis: their length is unknown and the card can be narrower than the header

snippets.note: the exported accent colour and progress float
the progress fill: componentWidth() * clamp(0, 1, @progress), safe for any host value

check.describe: Defaults show Ada Lovelace with a purple avatar and a 65% bar; variables {name: Grace Hopper, subtitle: COBOL committee, accent: #FF26A69A, progress: 0.3} change all four. Resized, the text column takes the remaining width (weight 1): the progress track stretches, and a name or subtitle too long for a narrow card ends in an ellipsis.

pitfalls: clamp takes the value last: clamp(0, 1, @progress). clamp(@progress, 0, 1) always gives 0 (the middle argument is the maximum)
resources.variables entries are exported only with "export": true, while resources.colors entries are exported unless "export": false
A weighted child ignores the row's spacedBy (the row overflows by the gap): space the avatar from the text column with a fixed 16 dp spacer box instead
textFromFloat pads the number to `whole` digits with leading spaces; flags 4 (no leading pad) keeps "30% complete" flush with the bar
A host string in a narrow card wraps word by word and pushes the rest of the column out of the card unless it is limited to one line
